# How this specification was generated

**The specification is assembled from hand-written templates. No part of it is generated prose.**

The scope was read by an OpenAI model, which proposed the answers below. The documents themselves are assembled from templates — an OpenAI model wrote none of them.

---

## What produced it

| # | Step | A model? | What it reads |
|---|---|:---:|---|
| 1 | **You describe the work** — You write a paragraph or two, or upload documents. | no | Your words, kept verbatim as `scope.md`. |
| 2 | **Something reads the scope** — Proposes the application type, architecture pattern, domain packs, rigor tier, and which capability modules apply. Every proposal is shown with the phrase it came from, and every one is editable. | optionally | Your scope, and the list of 31 capability modules. |
| 3 | **Deterministic rules choose the documents** — Twenty answers decide which of the numbered documents exist, which domain packs are added, which sections are suppressed, and what a module forces back in. No judgement, no model — a lookup table with the reason recorded for every decision. | no | `03-TAILORING-RULES.md`, executable as `rules.py`. |
| 4 | **Templates are assembled** — Each selected document is read from disk, the capability modules inject their content at named anchors, suppressed sections are deleted, and placeholders are filled from your answers. | no | The hand-written templates and 914 module fragments in this repository. |
| 5 | **One document, then two folders** — The assembled documents are ordered by lifecycle phase into `SPECIFICATION.md`, then split by audience into a scope half and a technical half, with a folder per capability in each. | no | What step 4 produced. |

Only step 2 can involve a model, and only if a key is configured. Steps 3, 4 and 5 — the ones that decide what the document says — are a lookup table and a text substitution.

## Why that matters

| | |
|---|---|
| **Every sentence exists in this repository before you ask for it** | The documents come from `_spec/`, `_architecture/`, `_extensions/` and `_modules/` — 914 fragments, written and reviewed by people. You can read them without running anything. |
| **The same answers always produce the same specification** | The rules are a lookup table. Generate twice with the same answers and the output is identical, byte for byte — which is not a property anything model-written has. |
| **A model, when configured, only proposes which templates apply** | It answers the twenty questions and names modules. It writes nothing that reaches the document, and every proposal is shown with its reason and stays editable. |
| **Without a key, nothing leaves the machine** | The keyword analyser needs no network. Your scope stays where you typed it. |
| **What is missing is left visible, not filled in** | `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` and `DECISION REQUIRED` are the generator declining to invent. A model asked to finish a document would have written something plausible there instead, and that is the failure this is built to avoid. |

`SPEC-PROFILE.md` in this download lists every document included and excluded, with the reason for each. `spec-profile.json` holds the exact answers, so regenerating this specification is one step rather than twenty questions again.

---

*If a sentence in this specification looks wrong, it is wrong in a template in the builder's repository, and fixing it there fixes it for everybody. That is the point of templates over generation.*
